correctness.rationale: The finite Shrikhande Cayley graph and all 32 triangles are constructed explicitly. Both exhaustive face tests agree on 8950 nonempty faces. A 4465-pair matching has critical-cell counts (one 0-cell, five 5-cells, fourteen 6-cells); the entire 48272-edge directed Hasse graph is proven acyclic by exhaustive sort. An exactly signed Morse 5x14 matrix has a displayed rank-five determinant-one minor, so all 5-cell attachments cancel and nine six-spheres remain. The lack of lower cells and π5(∨5S5)=Z5 justify this as homotopy rather than only homology. Raw mod-two boundary ranks independently corroborate the result, but do not substitute for the integral certificate.

value.rationale: This natural clique-free filtration step on a canonical 16-vertex torus triangulation has an exact and nonobvious homotopy type concentrated in dimension six despite facets of dimensions six, seven and eight. It gives a genuinely distinct, calculable topological invariant for the strongly regular Shrikhande graph in comparison with the previously computed rook counterpart, although both have the same 16 vertices, 48 edges and 32 triangles. The precise nine-sphere homotopy classification is not supplied by existing CF2 or matching-complex calculations and is useful as a reproducible benchmark for higher clique-free graph topology.
